plan.topic: Tirzepatide not working yet? Why trial weight loss built gradually over months rather than weeks
plan.angle: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) not working yet? In SURMOUNT-1 (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes), average weight loss built over months, not weeks, and kept going late into the 72 weeks. Use one exactly copied NEJM figure with dose arm, n per arm, placebo comparator, estimand and timepoint. One line: the trial raised the dose gradually by design, and your prescriber decides yours, never adjust it yourself. Averages, not predictions. One GI side-effects line. Don't change, stop or switch on your own; ask your prescriber about your progress. Prescriber line. Run it the day after L1 publishes, with the L1 'Full breakdown' CTA.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Not Working Yet? What the Trial Shows #shorts
plan.why: Spin-off of L1 that sends viewers to today's long-form. It names the drug ('tirzepatide' titles: median 83) and makes a myth-busting point that's true. | fact-check: Good myth correction, and SURMOUNT-1 supports it: weight loss built over months and was still going at the later timepoints. Risk: a 'not working yet?' frame can push frustrated viewers toward raising the dose themselves, microdosing or gray-market products. The Short must say plainly that the trial's gradual dose increase was part of the design and is set by the prescriber, with no numbers or schedule. Use one number exactly as printed in NEJM (e.g. mean % change at week 72 for one named dose vs placebo, with that arm's n and the placebo n, and the estimand), or an earlier timepoint only if the paper reports it in numbers. Don't add an early-weeks number read off the graph. The title has no number, OK. Scheduling: the playbook says funnel Shorts run the day after their long-form. Publish S2 after L1 is live so the 'Full breakdown' CTA is valid. If it runs before, end on 'follow for more' as specified. Keep 'averages, not predictions', one GI line, 'don't change, stop or switch on your own; ask your prescriber about your progress' and the prescriber line.

package.title: Tirzepatide Not Working Yet? Why Trial Loss Took Months #shorts
package.description:
Follow @InforMedLab for more.

In SURMOUNT-1 (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes), tirzepatide 15mg plus lifestyle counseling (n=630) averaged a 20.9% weight loss at week 72 vs 3.1% on placebo (n=643) — a treatment-regimen estimate; averages, not predictions. Loss built gradually over months, not weeks. Most common side effects were gastrointestinal (nausea, diarrhea), mostly mild-to-moderate, mainly during dose increases. Don't change, stop or switch your medicine on your own.

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
- Jastreboff AM et al., "Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity," NEJM, 2022: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2206038
- SURMOUNT-1 trial summary, American College of Cardiology, 2022: https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/Clinical-Trials/2022/08/04/15/32/SURMOUNT-1
- NCT04184622 (SURMOUNT-1), ClinicalTrials.gov: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04184622

script.cta: Full breakdown: How Long Does Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Take to Work? On our channel. Publish this Short only after L1 is live under exactly that title. Put the L1 link in the pinned comment and in the first line of the description. If L1 isn't live yet, change the s8 narration to "Follow for more." and its on-screen text to "Follow for more".

factcheck.summary: This Short passes. Every factual claim checks out against SURMOUNT-1 (Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2022, PMID 35658024). I confirmed the abstract through Europe PMC: 2,539 adults with obesity, 72 weeks, a 20-week dose-raising phase, and average weight change of −15.0%, −19.5% and −20.9% on 5, 10 and 15 mg versus −3.1% on placebo. It also says the side effects were mostly gastrointestinal and mostly mild to moderate during dose increases. The ACC trial summary confirms the group sizes: 15 mg n=630 and placebo n=643. It also confirms doses started at 2.5 mg and went up by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks, and that the trial drug was given on top of lifestyle intervention. ClinicalTrials.gov confirms NCT04184622, the population (no type 2 diabetes; obesity, or overweight with weight-related conditions) and the 4 Dec 2019 start date. The −20.9% is the treatment-regimen figure, as the script says. Saying the average kept falling well after the 20-week dose-raising phase matches the trial's 72-week result. The safety pieces are all there: no dose schedule, a 'don't change, stop or switch on your own' line, the prescriber line, and the 'averages, not predictions' line. The hook is answered within about 10 seconds, and the s8 call to action depends on L1 being live, which is the right rule. There are three small fixes, below.

issues.claim: Tirzepatide 15 mg −20.9% vs placebo −3.1% at week 72 (averages)
issues.problem: For someone watching muted, the stat card doesn't say who was studied (adults with obesity or overweight, without diabetes). It also doesn't flag that 15 mg was the top dose, so viewers on lower doses may hold themselves to the best result.
issues.fix: on_screen_text: "Top dose 15 mg −20.9% vs placebo −3.1%, week 72 (adults without diabetes; averages)". stat_label: "Average weight change, tirzepatide 15 mg (top dose), adults without diabetes, week 72"

issues.claim: the fifteen milligram tirzepatide group … averaged a twenty point nine percent drop
issues.problem: Only the top-dose result is given. Most viewers who think it's 'not working yet' are probably on lower doses. Saying that's the highest trial dose sets fairer expectations without giving a dose schedule.
issues.fix: Change "the fifteen milligram tirzepatide group" to "the top-dose fifteen milligram tirzepatide group".

issues.problem: This line is our own safety advice. It isn't in SURMOUNT-1 or on ClinicalTrials.gov, so the source tag covers more than the source says. Only the 'doses rose gradually, by design' part is supported.
issues.fix: Keep the source_ids ["nejm-surmount1-2022", "ctgov-surmount1"] for the dose-raising clause only, and note that 'Only your prescriber adjusts yours' is our own advice with no source tag. Any on-screen source tag should sit on the dose-raising beat, not on 'Prescriber sets your dose'.

audio.soundNotes: Music sits well (-13.5dB under voice) so only a small +1dB nudge to lift pause sections toward -14dB; left under-speech level alone per guidance. Boosted the two anemic transition swells at 15.3s and 46.44s (they measured -26/-32dB, inaudible) and the stat-reveal "ding" at 33.19s for a satisfying payoff, while trimming the over-loud, over-clustered swoosh/blip trio at 47.0-47.1s and thinning redundant duplicate ticks/bubbles/swooshes across several dense clusters. Pulled back the SFX around the "don't adjust on your own" and "talk to your prescriber" safety lines (64-67s) and replaced some of that density with a single subtle low custom tone to keep the serious moment uncluttered; added two more custom accents (a rising swell at the "kept falling for months" reveal and a crisp chime at the -20.9% stat) to make the key beats land without adding clutter.
